findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the mechanism by which the fixture detects a freshly-started container vs. a stale one — for example, `jira-dc-up` writes a timestamp label on the container (`docker label jira-dc-started-at=<epoch>`), and the fixture reads that label at startup and skips/fails if it was created before the current process started.

An implementer must invent how the fixture determines whether the container it sees was freshly started by `--force-recreate` vs. a leftover from an interrupted previous run — with no guidance, an implementer could use a startup timestamp comparison, a sentinel file in the container, a container label, or simply skip the check entirely.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the `allow_insecure` contradiction: either update the parent epic's Approach §7 to reassign the obligation to J6/J7 (which re-stales the parent's plan-review attestation and requires its re-review), or restore the AC in J5 requiring harness smoke tests to set `allow_insecure = true` and assert the warning fires — the parent wins on any conflict.
evidence: Parent e369 Approach §7: 'The J5 harness is the intended allow_insecure case, not an exception to it. The Dockerized Jira serves plain http://localhost:2990/jira, so every live test against it sets allow_insecure = true explicitly and asserts the warning is emitted.'

The parent names J5 as the story that exercises the allow_insecure override; the leaf explicitly disclaims it. One of them must be wrong per the CONFLICT RULE (parent wins).
findings.finding: The leaf explicitly reassigns the `allow_insecure = true` obligation away from J5 to J6/J7, directly contradicting the parent epic's Approach §7, which states: 'The J5 harness is the intended allow_insecure case, not an exception to it. The Dockerized Jira serves plain http://localhost:2990/jira, so every live test against it sets allow_insecure = true explicitly and asserts the warning is emitted.' The parent is authoritative; the leaf cannot unilaterally re-assign a requirement the parent placed on it.

scenarios: J6/J7 are implemented against this harness without any test in J5 asserting the allow_insecure warning fires — the parent's stated coverage guarantee is never delivered.
A code reviewer checking J5's AC list finds no allow_insecure verification, looks at the parent, and sees an unresolved contradiction that requires re-opening J5 after J6 is closed.
findings.suggested_fix: If the leaf's reasoning is correct (J5 speaks raw REST v2 and never constructs rebar's DC backend, so no validator is on its path), update the parent epic §7 to read 'every live test in J6/J7 that constructs rebar's DC backend against this harness sets allow_insecure = true and asserts the warning is emitted' — then the leaf's dismissal is a consistent narrowing rather than a contradiction. Plan states: 'this harness proves REST v2 protocol semantics' — but the ADAPTER uses v3, so the harness cannot prove the adapter works
Evidence class: Contradicted — the environment (Jira DC 8.17.1) falsifies the claim that driving the adapter against it proves adapter correctness
findings.finding: The adapter code this harness is intended to verify uses Cloud-era `/rest/api/3/` endpoints throughout (`POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with `nextPageToken` cursor pagination, `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}`, `POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions`, `GET /rest/api/3/user/assignable/search`, `PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee`), but Jira Server/DC 8.17.1 does not serve the v3 API surface — only v2. When J6/J7 drive the actual adapter against this harness, every `/rest/api/3/` call will fail (404/405), meaning the harness cannot verify the adapter code it was designed to test. The smoke tests themselves use `/rest/api/2/` directly and will succeed, but that proves the instance is up, not that the adapter works.
findings.location: Approach section ('this story proves REST v2 protocol semantics'); Scope ('a smoke test creates and reads back an issue via REST v2'); Testing section ('happy path: creates and reads back one issue through raw REST v2'); the stated purpose is to give J6/J7 'something real to be verified against'
scenarios: J6 wires the DC adapter against the harness and every `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map`, `get_issue_by_rest`, `transition_issue_by_name`, `validate_assignee_exists` call returns HTTP 404, making J6's live tests fail not because the adapter logic is wrong but because the test infrastructure uses the wrong API version.
A future maintainer reads 'the harness proves REST v2 protocol semantics' and concludes the adapter is validated, not realising the adapter itself uses v3.

findings.finding: The plan asserts that living under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` satisfies the gating requirement 'for free' via the conftest structural backstop — but only describes the marker auto-application and hard-fail-misplacement behavior. findings.finding: `tests/external/conftest.py`'s `_live_jira_ready` sentinel pattern and `jira_live` auto-marker mechanism are unenumerated consumers. findings.finding: `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` is an unenumerated consumer: it already runs `pytest -m external tests/external -q`, which will collect all new tests under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`. findings.finding: The existing external-integration.yml workflow has no Docker build/run/teardown steps and requires an LLM API key as a hard prerequisite. The plan places the Jira DC harness under tests/external/ so it runs from this workflow, but does not address how the workflow is extended: the Jira DC harness needs docker build, docker compose up, a 20-minute readiness wait, and docker compose down — none of which exist in the current `external` job. The plan's scope adds a `jira-dc-up` Makefile target but says nothing about the CI workflow modification needed to wire it.
findings.location: Scope section ('Makefile — a jira-dc-up target only'); Testing section; Approach section ('gating oracle: external-integration.yml')

findings.finding: The existing `external-integration.yml` workflow already runs `pytest -m external tests/external -q` (line 141), which will auto-collect all new tests under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`.
